title: Ingredients
description: Everything a recipe can call for, and what people can keep in their bar. The order in the file is the order the app shows.

id.description: Stable id. Recipes and people's bars refer to it, so it never changes once published.

category.description: Kind of ingredient. Missing a spirit or liqueur counts heavily against a recipe; missing a juice or fresh item counts less, because it is a quick shop.

family.description: Loose group of ingredients that can stand in for each other at a stretch (whiskey, rum, amaro). A stand-in from the same family counts as a rough substitute.

substitutes.description: Ingredient ids that work well in place of this one (rye for bourbon). Counts as a close substitute. One-way: list it on both if it works both ways.

shelfLifeDays.description: Roughly how many days it stays good once opened (vermouth about six weeks, fino sherry two). Opened bottles near or past this are pushed up the recommendations.

specialty.description: A bottle most bars buy for one or two drinks and then struggle to finish (crème de violette, falernum). Recipes that use one up get a boost.

staple.description: Something most people have or can grab on the way home (citrus, simple syrup, soda). Missing it barely counts against a recipe.

aliases.description: Other names people search by, lowercase ("triple sec" for Cointreau).
